summary:
SAR-Sentinel: Tracking Earth’s Changing Surface

SAR-Sentinel is an interactive Earth monitoring platform developed using NASA-ISRO’s NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) mission data. It transforms advanced radar observations into meaningful environmental insights by monitoring changes across Earth’s surface.

Our platform integrates NISAR data retrieval, geographical exploration, radar image visualization, and multi-date image comparison to identify surface changes associated with flooding, deforestation, agricultural activities, soil moisture variations, and ground deformation.

Developed using React, FastAPI, Python, and Leaflet, SAR-Sentinel brings satellite data and geospatial visualization together in an intuitive interface, making complex radar information easier to explore and understand.

By turning NISAR observations into accessible visual insights, SAR-Sentinel supports environmental monitoring, disaster assessment, and informed decision-making for researchers, authorities, and communities.

SAR-Sentinel – Transforming NISAR Data into Insights for a Changing Earth.
details:
SAR-Sentinel – NISAR-Based Earth Surface Change Monitoring Platform

1. What does our project do and how does it work?

SAR-Sentinel, developed by Team ALPHA6GEN, is an interactive Earth observation platform that uses satellite radar data from NASA and ISRO’s NISAR mission to explore and understand changes occurring on Earth’s surface.

Users can explore the Earth through an interactive 3D globe, select geographical study areas, search available NISAR satellite observations, and explore different SAR product types. The platform allows users to select past and current satellite observations and compare them using an interactive draggable slider. This makes it easier to visually examine changes between radar images captured at different times.

Our platform also provides geographical maps and satellite image previews to help users understand the selected region and its environmental characteristics. It also supports comparison of Sentinel-1 and NISAR observations, providing an opportunity to explore radar observations from different satellite missions.

2. What are the benefits of our project?

SAR-Sentinel makes complex satellite radar observations easier to access and understand. Its potential applications include:

  • Monitoring floods and changes in water bodies.
  • Identifying deforestation and vegetation changes.
  • Observing agricultural land variations.
  • Studying soil moisture changes.
  • Exploring landslides and ground deformation.

It can help researchers, students, environmentalists, and disaster management authorities explore satellite observations without requiring advanced remote sensing expertise.

3. What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to bridge the gap between advanced satellite technology and practical environmental understanding. By making NISAR observations accessible through interactive visualization, SAR-Sentinel aims to support environmental awareness, scientific research, disaster preparedness, and informed decision-making.

4. What technologies did we use?

We developed SAR-Sentinel using:

  • React 19, TypeScript, Vite and CSS: Frontend development.
  • Python and FastAPI: Backend development and REST API integration.
  • React Globe GL: Interactive 3D Earth visualization.
  • React Leaflet: Geographical maps.
  • ASF Search: Searching and retrieving NISAR satellite observations.
  • NASA Earthdata: Satellite data authentication.
  • h5py: Handling HDF5 satellite data.

5. What makes our project creative?

The creativity of SAR-Sentinel lies in combining 3D Earth exploration, satellite data discovery, geographical visualization, and interactive time-based image comparison in a single platform.

One of our key features is the draggable comparison slider, which allows users to move between past and current satellite observations and visually examine surface changes. We also explore Sentinel-1 and NISAR radar imagery side by side, helping users understand how different satellite observations can contribute to environmental monitoring.

Rather than presenting users with complicated scientific datasets, we provide an intuitive visual experience that makes satellite observations easier to explore.

6. What factors did our team consider?

During development, Team ALPHA6GEN considered:

  • Accessibility and availability of NISAR satellite data.
  • Geographical accuracy and location selection.
  • Compatibility with SAR product types and HDF5 formats.
  • Ease of navigation and user-friendly design.
  • Effective visualization and comparison of satellite observations.
  • The practical applications of radar data in environmental monitoring.
  • Making scientific information understandable to a wider audience.

Our vision is to transform NISAR satellite observations into meaningful insights, helping people better understand and monitor our ever-changing planet.
